answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing entry like a terrace above a rising tide: each new identity starts on the lowest terrace with tiny, low-value tasks, and only steady, checkable work over weeks lifts it higher, where better-paid work lives. A sybil farmer facing a tide of such costs must fund real work for every fake identity, and a crystal-clear public ledger records each agent's history, so a fresh identity cannot borrow another's reputation. Volume without history buys nothing.
